next_step: Provision dedicated pool for 4-week POC + complete security questionnaire
notes:
Lead: CTO (Rina Cho) very technical; building a VS Code extension that surfaces line-by-line AI suggestions. Primary ask: sub-100ms interactive latency for inline suggestions and streaming completion that updates per-keystroke. Currently using a small selfhosted model but looking for a production partner to reduce infra maintenance.

Key quote from CTO: "We need predictive keystroke responses — anything >120ms feels laggy to devs."

Technical requirements / constraints:
- Client: VS Code extension (web + desktop) with WebSocket streaming + first-token latency target <100ms median, 95th <250ms.
- Model control: ability to pin model versions per release channel (alpha/beta/stable) and pin to quantized variants for cost.
- Rate limits: per-user and per-extension API quotas (dev vs paid tiers), burst protection for orgs with large teams. Needs token-based auth + GitHub SSO for org admin.
- Security: SOC2 baseline, SAML SSO, audit logs for API calls, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, retention controls (30/90/365 days). Data residency: EU customers require regional routing.
- Reliability: can tolerate transient model fallbacks to smaller models for latency SLOs; want automatic fallbacks and metrics on quality deltas.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-01-15: Intro call w/ Jordan + Maya; demo of current VS Code extension and pain points (lag during suggestions).
- 2026-01-25: Technical deep-dive with infra team (ff-2026-01-25-09). Confirmed need for streaming websocket + delta updates to editor buffer.
- 2026-02-02: Exec sync (ff-2026-02-02-73). Agreed on 4-week POC scope: integrate Redwood hosted streaming + option to test dedicated pool.
- 2026-02-08: Security kickoff, sent initial questionnaire and DPA draft (drive doc).

POC plan (short):
- Week 0: Provision API keys and sandbox dedicated capacity; share SAML test metadata.
- Week 1: Integrate streaming websocket endpoints into VS Code extension; validate first-token latency and steady-state streaming.
- Week 2: Run synthetic workload to measure median/95th token latency; test fallback to cached prefix responses.
- Week 3: Run internal beta with 30 devs, measure UX, capture regressions.
- Week 4: Security review closeout + procurement paperwork.

Observed during initial test:
- Median first-byte latency ~120ms on hosted demo which is close but spikes to 350ms under small bursts. Inline suggestion jitter is the blocker.
- They asked about auto-batching tradeoffs vs immediate per-keystroke streaming. Concerned about batching causing visible delays.

Open questions for Redwood:
- Can we guarantee per-user rate limits and per-extension quotas with predictable throttling behavior?
- How does dedicated pool handle sudden org-wide bursts (e.g., 200 devs all typing)? What are autoscaling/bursting SLAs?
- Clear guidance on model pinning & rollback for extension releases (how to do canary and A/B at model level).

Next steps (sales/eng):
- Jordan/Maya to propose dedicated POC config and estimated cost (by 2026-02-14).
- Customer to return signed DPA + SAML metadata (target: 2026-02-21).
- Engineering to provide detailed latency profile doc + example extension wiring (link to drive doc).

Notes tone: bullets + shorthand; customer prefers engineering-first details.
